chunks: And by this chain, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the sins of the believers are forgiven for them, so let the believer work for what he is starting anew; indeed, they are not except for the people of faith.

key_terms.لِمَا يَسْتَأْنِفُ: for what he is starting anew / to begin fresh

ai.seo_question: What is the status of believers' sins according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Fadail al-Shia, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the forgiveness of sins is a specific privilege reserved exclusively for the 'people of faith' (ahl al-iman), distinguishing them from others. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the inseparable link between true belief (iman) and divine mercy, encouraging believers to renew their spiritual efforts with the confidence that their past transgressions are covered by this covenantal grace.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters)… from al-Hasan in Mahboub from al-Alaa from Mohammed bin Muslim that Abu Ja’far (a) said:
The sins of the believers are already forgiven. Hence, a believer should put a new start. This is surely granted for the people of faith exclusively.
